subject: Mathematics
source: Edexcel (Pearson) GCSE (9-1) Mathematics 1MA1 specification (2015 onwards) — Y11 spec points across Algebra, Ratio/Proportion, Geometry, Probability and Statistics. Codes follow Edexcel reference numbering.

specPoints.specTitle: Manipulate algebraic expressions including expanding products of two or more binomials and factorising quadratic expressions of the form ax^2 + bx + c (HT for ax^2 with a > 1)
Simplify and manipulate algebraic fractions (HT only)
Solve linear equations in one unknown, including with the unknown on both sides
Solve quadratic equations algebraically by factorising, completing the square (HT) and using the quadratic formula (HT)
Solve two simultaneous equations in two variables algebraically and graphically; including one linear, one quadratic (HT)
Solve linear inequalities; represent the solution set on a number line and using set notation; solve quadratic inequalities (HT)
Plot and interpret straight-line graphs; identify gradient and intercept; identify parallel lines and perpendicular lines (HT for perpendicular)
Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs of linear, quadratic, simple cubic, reciprocal y = a/x, exponential a^x (HT) and trigonometric functions (HT)
Sketch translations and reflections of given functions (HT only)
Plot and interpret graphs in real contexts including distance-time, velocity-time and financial contexts; estimate gradients and areas under non-linear graphs (HT)
Generate terms of arithmetic sequences and geometric sequences; deduce nth term expressions for linear and quadratic sequences (HT for quadratic)
Find approximate solutions to equations numerically using iteration (HT only)
Use ratio notation; reduce a ratio to simplest form; divide a quantity into a given ratio
Express the division of a quantity in a given ratio as a fraction or percentage of the whole
Solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion, including graphical and algebraic representations
Calculate compound measures, including pressure, density and rates of flow
Solve percentage problems including percentage change, percentage profit/loss, simple interest, compound interest, repeated percentage change and reverse percentages
Set up, solve and interpret growth and decay problems including compound interest
Convert between related compound units (speed, rates of pay, prices, density, pressure)
Apply the properties of angles at a point, on a straight line, in a triangle and in any polygon
Apply the standard congruence conditions and similarity relationships, including length, area and volume scale factors
Apply Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometric ratios in 2D triangles; apply Pythagoras and trigonometry in 3D problems (HT for 3D)
Use the sine rule and cosine rule and the formula area = ½ab sin C (HT only)
Identify, describe and construct congruent and similar shapes by rotation, reflection, translation and enlargement (including fractional and negative scale factors — HT for negative)
Calculate perimeters and areas of polygons, circles and composite shapes; calculate arc lengths, sector areas and angles
Calculate surface areas and volumes of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres
Apply circle theorems including angle at centre, angle in semicircle, angles in same segment, alternate segment theorem (HT only)
Apply addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors; use vectors in geometric arguments and proofs (HT for proofs)
Record, describe and analyse the frequency of outcomes of simple probability experiments
Apply ideas of randomness, fairness and equally likely events
Calculate probabilities of independent and dependent combined events using tree diagrams and Venn diagrams (HT for dependent and conditional)
Calculate and interpret conditional probabilities (HT only)
Construct and interpret tables, charts and diagrams: bar charts, pie charts, pictograms, frequency tables, frequency polygons, time series
Interpret, analyse and compare distributions through measures of central tendency, spread, and graphical representation including box plots and cumulative frequency
Construct and interpret histograms with equal and unequal class widths (HT for unequal)
Use scatter graphs to identify correlation and lines of best fit; interpolate and extrapolate apparent trends with awareness of limits
Apply statistics to describe a population, including sampling techniques and bias awareness (HT only for stratified sampling)
